EN: Kerbal pilots and many probes can use the Stability Assist System (S.A.S.). This can \nhelp to keep your vessel pointed in the desired direction. The S.A.S. modes can be \nseen to the left of the NavBall here.
S.A.S. uses control sources to apply force to get you back on target. If there's not enough force you \nmay need more control parts, or a different design.
Note: These will consume resources, \nyou need to be mindful if you leave \nS.A.S. engaged for a long time.
More advanced modes allow you to \ntarget other directions, as shown \nwith the matching NavBall markers.
At its most basic, S.A.S. will hold the \nheading of your vessel, this is called \nstability mode.
Carrying unneeded equipment with you uses much more fuel. Most rockets use stages to get rid of \nused SRBs, engines, fuel tanks or other parts that are no longer required.
Note: Staging while engines are still running can have explosive consequences.

Another benefit is that you are not 
going to try and land the whole 
launch vessel. Just the important 
parts.
Staging starts at the highest stage \nnumber. Each time you "stage" it \nactivates the next one.

Trying to add these manually 
is possible, but it will never be 
exactly balanced. If you do it 
manually you will likely require 
constant inputs to stay on 
course.
Using radial symmetry and snap you can quickly add 2, 3, 4, etc \nparts around the center of the rocket, to maintain good balance.
When attaching components to vessels, the symmetry tools \ncan help you keep things aligned with the CoM, CoT and CoL.
<color=#ef2929>Note: </color>There is also mirror \nsymmetry, which is especially \nuseful for building planes.

When performing science activities it is key to understand the location 
for the activity. These involve where you are - planet/biome - and what 
you're doing - flying, orbiting, landed, etc. 

This combination of situation, planet and biome is the subject of an 
experiment - eg. landed at Minmus flats.

Science points (or Science) are needed to research technology areas 
and unlock their related parts. These points are generated primarily 
through experiment and observation throughout the solar system. 

You will also get some for passing milestones and completing some 
types of contracts.

The scientific method is an all consuming passion for many kerbals, 
and luckily also a key to unlocking many technological advances for 
spaceflight. 

An important function of your space program is to see how you can 
advance science and technology for Kerbalkind.

By choosing "Keep Experiment" the report will be 
stored to be recovered with the kerbal or vessel on 
Kerbin's surface.

This usually nets you the best Science return, and is 
the only way to extract all the possible Science from 
any experiment and subject combination.

When you perform activities a report 
with the data is generated. 

The primary method to extract the 
Science from that data, and advance 
kerbal knowledge, is to get the data 
back to Kerbin.
